title: The Friendly Monster Under the Bed
summary: One night, Iván hears a noise under his bed. A monster lives there, and it turns out the monster is scared of the dark. And of children.

scenes.text:
Iván already had his pyjamas on, he had already brushed his teeth, and he had already asked for one last glass of water.

Dad switched off the light.

"Leave the door open," Iván asked. "Just a little bit."

Dad left it open just a little bit, and a thread of light from the hallway came into the room.

Iván pulled the covers up to his ears. He didn't like the dark one bit.

Everything was quiet. And then, from under the bed, came a noise.

"Atchoo!"

Iván went stiff as a board.

Slowly, very slowly, he took the torch out from under his pillow. He leaned over the edge of the bed. And he shone it.

Between an old ball and a slipper, there were two enormous eyes.

They were the eyes of a monster. A blue, furry monster with two little round ears. He was curled up in a ball, hugging his knees, and wobbling like a jelly.

"Please," whispered the monster. "Don't hurt me."

Iván blinked. The monster was much more scared than he was.

"I won't hurt you," said Iván. "What's your name?"

"Grumo."

"And why are you shaking, Grumo?"

The monster looked around, as if he were embarrassed.

"It's very dark down here," he said. "And the house makes funny noises at night. And besides…" He lowered his voice. "My mum says that sometimes children turn up under beds."

Iván covered his mouth. But he couldn't hold it in, and out came a giggle.

Grumo looked offended. Then he started laughing too.

"Are you scared of the dark as well?" asked Grumo.

"A little bit," said Iván. "That's why I leave the door open."

"What funny noises?" asked Iván.

The two of them went very quiet, listening.

Something was humming in the kitchen, softly, without stopping.

"That's the fridge," said Iván. "It purrs all night, like a big cat."

Something went glug, glug, glug inside the wall.

"That's the water going through the pipes. It's going to the neighbours' bath."

And something tapped gently on the window.

"And that's the wind," said Iván, "coming to see if we're asleep yet."

Grumo opened his eyes very wide. Every noise, once it had a name, was less scary.

"Hey," he said. "You know a lot about the night."

That night, Grumo didn't stay under the bed.

He climbed up very quietly and curled up at Iván's feet, on top of the blanket. Iván lent him his teddy, the softest one, so he'd have something to hug.

"Goodnight, Grumo."

"Goodnight, Iván."

After a while, from the foot of the bed, there came a blue, furry snore.

Iván smiled in the dark. He wasn't scared any more. Now he knew who was there.

And since that night, there's no need to leave the door open.
